title: Reconcile with what CloudWatch says now
description:
**Reworked 2026-11-04:** Ryan reversed the architecture. No new AWS account and no central service; see docs/notifications-plan.md in AnthusAI/Caducus.

**Milestone:** M1, first slice

**Goal.** As an operator, I hear about alarms already firing when the listener starts, and about any state change whose event was lost. On 2026-11-04 seven alarms in papyrus-production were already in ALARM; state-change events alone would never mention them.

**Build.**
- `src/caducus/notify/reconcile.py`, `handlers/reconcile.py`: takes the current alarms (host passes `describe-alarms` pages), compares with `INCIDENT#` rows, and feeds synthetic transitions through the normal incident path with stable event ids, so a real event for the same change dedupes.
- First run opens incidents for what is firing, grouped like any storm, so day one is one or two messages.
- The host schedules it. Works against fakes; moto for the adapter.

**Acceptance.**
Behave features green; the first run against a fixture of 47 alarms, 7 firing, makes one incident per firing alarm and grouped messages.

**Depends on:** kanbus-9a3b85
**Related:** PPY-e92c8e

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Reconcile
  Scenario: Alarms already firing at start
    Given an alarm is in ALARM and has no incident
    When reconciliation runs
    Then an incident opens and one message goes out

  Scenario: A lost clearing event
    Given an open incident whose alarm is now OK
    When reconciliation runs
    Then the hold-down starts as if the event had arrived

  Scenario: The real event arrives too
    Given reconciliation opened an incident
    When the state-change event for it arrives
    Then no second message goes out
```
